name: AHS – Image to WebP Converter
author: ahsdeveloper

sections.description:
AHS – Image to WebP Converter automatically converts uploaded images into the modern WebP format, helping improve website speed, reduce bandwidth usage, and boost PageSpeed scores.

The plugin works seamlessly with standard WordPress hosting environments and requires no external services.

Features

  • Automatic Conversion: Converts JPG and PNG images to WebP on upload.
  • Bulk Conversion Tool: Convert existing images from the media library.
  • Conversion Statistics: View how many images have been optimized.
  • Configurable WebP Quality: Adjust image quality to balance size and clarity.
  • Modern Admin Interface: Clean dashboard with progress indicators.
  • Safe by Design: Original images are always preserved.

How It Works

When an image is uploaded, the plugin generates a WebP version alongside the original image using WordPress’s native image handling system. Original files are never deleted, ensuring full compatibility with all themes and browsers.

The plugin does not require any external account or third-party service to function.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress
  3. Navigate to Settings → Image to WebP
  4. Configure your preferred WebP quality and run bulk conversion if needed
sections.faq:
Does this plugin replace original images?

No. Original images are kept intact. WebP files are generated alongside them.

Which image formats are supported?

Currently supported formats:
* JPEG / JPG
* PNG

Does this plugin work on most hosting environments?

Yes. The plugin works on standard WordPress hosting setups without requiring special server configuration.

Is the plugin compatible with caching and CDN plugins?

Yes. Generated WebP files are stored locally and work with most caching and CDN setups.

Does this plugin require an internet connection or external API?

No. All image processing is performed locally on your server.
